title: Arm injury
dispatch: Respond to an adult cut by broken glass in a workshop.
presentation: A 34-year-old is seated beside a broken window, holding a bleeding forearm. A partner and bleeding-control supplies are available.

findings.breathing: Breathing spontaneously; chest movement is adequate.
findings.circulation: Blood flows rapidly from a deep forearm wound. Skin is pale and clammy; the radial pulse is rapid and weak.
findings.vitals: Authored initial values: pulse 124/min; respirations 24/min; BP 92/60 mmHg. These values do not update automatically.
findings.history: The injury happened minutes ago. The patient reports dizziness; further history is not specified.
findings.secondary: Deep forearm laceration; no embedded object or other major wound is found in this case.

goals.label: Escalate persistent major limb bleeding control

pressure.text: In this case, firm direct pressure slows the bleeding, but it continues. Your partner has a tourniquet ready.

tourniquet.text: Authored outcome after correct application: external bleeding stops. The patient remains pale; reassess circulation.

setFindings.circulation: External bleeding is controlled. Skin remains pale and clammy; the pulse remains rapid and weak.

delay.text: After the delay, the patient is more confused and the bleeding continues unless already controlled.

setFindings.responsiveness: The patient is confused after the delay.

review: Control major bleeding promptly. Persistent poor perfusion still requires ongoing assessment and timely transport.

title: Collision assessment
dispatch: Respond to an adult driver after a vehicle collision.
presentation: A 46-year-old remains in the secured vehicle after a frontal collision. They look pale and report abdominal pain; no external bleeding is apparent.

findings.responsiveness: Awake but slow to answer questions.
findings.airway: Patent; the patient can answer verbally.
findings.breathing: Rapid spontaneous breathing with chest movement.
findings.circulation: Cool, moist skin and a rapid, weak pulse; no major external bleeding is found.
findings.vitals: Authored initial values: pulse 128/min; respirations 26/min; BP 88/56 mmHg. These values do not update automatically.
findings.history: Seat-belted driver; abdominal pain began after impact. Other history is not specified.
findings.secondary: Abdominal bruising and tenderness. No externally bleeding wound is found.

delay.text: Following the delay, the patient becomes harder to keep engaged.

review: Internal bleeding may occur without an external wound. Assessment, transport, and reassessment remain priorities.

title: Bicycle fall
dispatch: Respond to an adult cyclist who struck their head.
presentation: A 29-year-old is lying beside a bicycle. They repeatedly ask what happened. No major external hemorrhage is visible.

findings.responsiveness: Awake but confused; repeatedly asks the same question.
findings.breathing: Currently spontaneous and adequate. Continue monitoring.
findings.circulation: A palpable pulse is present; no major external bleeding is found.
findings.vitals: Authored initial values: pulse 96/min; respirations 18/min; BP 126/78 mmHg. Reassess after any new findings.
findings.history: A witness reports a head strike. The patient cannot recall the event.
findings.secondary: Head abrasion and neck discomfort. The case does not establish a definitive diagnosis.

airwaySupport.text: Airway support is provided within training and protocol; the airway remains patent.

ventilation.text: When breathing is inadequate, assisted ventilation produces visible chest rise in this authored branch.

setFindings.breathing: Assisted ventilation is underway with visible chest rise; head injury remains a concern.

delay.text: During the delay, responsiveness declines and breathing becomes slow and inadequate.

setFindings.breathing: Slow, shallow respirations with inadequate chest rise.

review: Track changes in responsiveness and breathing. Supporting an immediate need does not remove the need for transport and continued care.

title: Chest impact
dispatch: Respond to an adult struck in the chest by heavy equipment.
presentation: A 41-year-old is seated against a wall. They report chest pain and can manage only short phrases. The scene has been secured.

findings.responsiveness: Awake, anxious, and struggling to speak full sentences.
findings.breathing: Shallow, inadequate chest rise with reduced movement on one side.
findings.circulation: The pulse is rapid; skin is pale. No major external bleeding is found.
findings.vitals: Authored initial values: pulse 118/min; respirations 30/min; BP 104/68 mmHg. Reassess rather than assuming these remain current.
findings.history: Heavy equipment struck the chest shortly before arrival.
findings.secondary: Chest bruising and tenderness; unequal chest movement. No open chest wound is present in this case.

ventilation.text: Authored outcome with effective assisted ventilation: visible chest rise is achieved. The injury remains serious.

setFindings.breathing: Assisted ventilation produces visible chest rise; the chest injury still requires urgent care.

delay.text: After the delay, the patient is more exhausted and breathing remains inadequate unless already supported.

review: Identify inadequate breathing, provide support within protocol, and continue assessment during timely transport.

title: Ladder fall
dispatch: Respond to an adult after a fall from a ladder.
presentation: A 52-year-old lies beside a ladder after a fall of about 10 feet. They complain loudly of ankle pain and also report neck discomfort.

findings.responsiveness: Alert and able to describe what happened.
findings.breathing: Spontaneous breathing with adequate chest rise.
findings.circulation: A pulse is present, skin is warm, and no major external bleeding is found.
findings.vitals: Authored initial values: pulse 100/min; respirations 20/min; BP 132/84 mmHg. Continue reassessing.
findings.history: The ladder slipped. The patient reports ankle and neck pain.
findings.secondary: Ankle swelling, neck pain, and new tingling in both hands; avoid focusing only on the limb injury.

delay.text: During the delay, the patient reports increasing tingling in both hands.

setFindings.secondary: Ankle swelling and neck pain persist; hand tingling is increasing.

review: A painful limb can distract from the primary assessment. Consider mechanism, neurologic findings, and ongoing reassessment.
